title: Reverse ETL: sending processed data back into operational tools

videos.script: A salesperson at Lantern opens a customer's record before a call. The record says nothing about how the customer buys. {{record}} The warehouse knows. It knows the orders, the revenue, and whether the customer has gone quiet. {{warehouse}} So far, every lesson has sent numbers to a screen somebody reads. This one sends them back, onto the customer's record. {{back}} That is reverse ETL. A model in SQL says what each record should hold. {{model}} A script compares it with what was sent last time, and sends only the difference. {{diff}} You will run it against a small pretend CRM on your own machine. It limits how fast you may call it, and it refuses values it does not know. {{crm}} Along the way, a customer asks to be forgotten. The copy in the CRM has to go too. {{erase}} And when a run fails halfway, the log says exactly which contacts did not arrive, and why. {{log}}
